Chapter 10. Sustaining Unconventional Thinking in a Conventional World.
So, here we are at the final step—how do you actually keep the habits and mindsets of unconventional thinking alive, especially when everything around you seems to reward playing it safe?
You know, it’s so easy to slip back into old routines, especially if you’re surrounded by people who love tradition or crave predictability. But if you want to keep that creative spark burning, here’s what really helps.
First, make a point to revisit those key principles that started you on this journey: keep questioning what you think you know, don’t shy away from uncertainty, pay attention to what motivates people, experiment often, and always look for different perspectives.
Another big help? Find—or even build—a community of people who think like you do. Folks who’ll encourage you, challenge your ideas, and help you see things in new ways.
And don’t underestimate the power of small reminders or personal rituals. Maybe it’s a note on your desk, a daily question you ask yourself, or a simple habit that keeps you curious and open.
Think of unconventional thinking like a campfire. If you want it to keep burning—especially when the wind picks up or the night gets cold—you’ve got to tend to it regularly. It needs your ongoing attention and care.
Leaders can make a huge difference here, by setting the example and creating safe spaces where people feel free to experiment and challenge the status quo. But really, anyone can help keep that spirit alive. You can do it just by asking thoughtful questions, sharing what you’re learning, and supporting others when they take a risk.
In the end, it’s not about being different just for the sake of it. It’s about staying open to new possibilities—about seeing the world as a place where better answers are always out there, just waiting to be found.
